Section 3 - Legal Basis for Processing
We process personal data only when we have a valid legal basis to do so. The legal bases we rely on are:
(cid:127) Contractual necessity — to provide the Services you have signed up for
(cid:127) Legitimate interests — for fraud prevention, security, and product improvement
(cid:127) Legal obligation — to comply with applicable laws and regulations
(cid:127) Consent — for marketing communications and optional analytics (you can withdraw at any time)
Where we rely on consent, you have the right to withdraw it at any time by contacting us at
privacy@techstartup.com. Withdrawal of consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing that
occurred before the withdrawal.

Section 6 - Data Sharing & Third Parties
We do not sell your personal data to any third parties. We share data only in the following circumstances:
Third Party Purpose Data Shared
Mixpanel Product analytics Usage data, events, device info
Razorpay Payment processing Transaction amount, user ID
Google (OAuth) Authentication Name, email, profile picture
AWS Cloud infrastructure & hosting All data stored on AWS servers
Intercom Customer support chat Name, email, support messages
Sentry Error monitoring Error logs, stack traces
All third-party processors are bound by data processing agreements that require them to handle data in
accordance with applicable privacy laws. We conduct annual reviews of our third-party processors to
ensure continued compliance.

Section 5 - User Rights
As a user of our platform, you have the following rights regarding your personal data. To exercise any of
these rights, please contact privacy@techstartup.com with the subject line 'Data Rights Request'. We aim
to respond to all requests within 14 business days.

requirements.analysis: The policy states that personal data is processed only on a valid legal basis and lists the bases, including consent with a withdrawal mechanism. However, it does not explicitly confirm that consent is freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous, which is required by Article 7(1).
requirements.fix_required: Add a clause stating that consent is freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous, and that data subjects can withdraw at any time.

priority_actions.action_required: Create a section outlining the handling, safeguards, and lawful bases for processing criminal conviction data as required by Article 10.
Add a 'Purpose Limitation' section documenting the specific purposes for processing and stating that data will not be used for incompatible purposes.
Document the specific lawful basis(es) required under Article 6(2) and how they are applied to processing activities.
Provide a detailed explanation of the consent requirements and other lawful bases stipulated in Article 6(3).
Include a section describing the lawful processing condition(s) outlined in Article 6(4) and how they are met.
Add a statement recognizing the free movement of personal data within the Union and how the organization complies with that principle.
Add a clause explicitly stating that processing outside the scope of Union law is excluded.
Include a reference to Regulation (EC) No 45/2001 and describe how its provisions are applied.
Document the specific procedural steps required by Art. 2 (4), such as consultation with supervisory authorities or impact assessments.
Include evidence of all applicable transfer mechanisms (e.g., adequacy decisions, BCRs) and a summary of the safeguards employed.
Add a statement affirming that all processing activities are undertaken with appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data.
Include a clause confirming that the organization respects and safeguards the fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals in all processing activities.
Add a section describing any automated processing activities, their purpose, and the safeguards or rights afforded to data subjects.
State the location of the controller/processor and confirm its establishment within the Union or provide the relevant legal basis for extraterritorial processing.
Add a section clarifying whether and how the service monitors behavior of persons in the Union.
